chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Mihran ibn Muhammad, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'There is no tyrant (jabbar) but with him is a believer, through whom Allah (Exalted and Majestic) protects the believers, and he is the one with the least share in the Hereafter, meaning the believer with the least share due to his companionship with the tyrant.'

key_terms.جَبَّار: Tyrant or despot, one who exercises power oppressively
key_terms.لِصُحْبَةِ الْجَبَّارِ: Due to the companionship of the tyrant

ai.seo_question: Why does a believer's share in the Hereafter decrease when they are with a tyrant?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith highlights the concept of 'hidden saints' (al-awliya al-khafiyyun) who reside within the courts of tyrants, serving as a divine shield for the community despite their own spiritual sacrifice. The scholar notes that their proximity to power and potential compromise in maintaining that position results in a diminished share of reward, illustrating the high cost of remaining among the unjust while preserving faith.
